reason_states.strengthening: Strengthening: the latest figure differs from the previous one by at least the material change, in the direction this reason needs

reason_states.unchanged: Unchanged: the latest figure differs from the previous one by less than the material change

risk_states.materialising: Materialising: the latest figure differs from the previous one by at least the material change, in the direction in which this risk grows
risk_states.receding: Receding: the latest figure differs from the previous one by at least the material change, in the other direction
risk_states.unchanged: Unchanged: the latest figure differs from the previous one by less than the material change
risk_states.not_tracked: Not tracked: no retained figure measures this risk

condition_states.happened: Happened: the figure it names is past the threshold in the stated direction (a figure equal to the threshold is not past it)
condition_states.not_happened: Not happened: the figure it names is not past the threshold in the stated direction (a figure equal to the threshold is not past it)

statement.text: Synthetic reading: in the Synthetic STEPS projection, total demand of 29,500 kt in 2030 exceeds total supply of 28,700 kt, so the physical balance runs short.

tables.why_not: Synthetic: demand and supply come from two publications on different bases, so no gap is computed.

about.text: Synthetic reading: the earlier edition put supply of 29,100 kt above demand of 28,750 kt in 2030; the newer edition puts demand of 29,500 kt above supply of 28,700 kt.

reasons.title: Synthetic clean-technology demand keeps growing
reasons.plain: Synthetic: more demand from clean technologies would widen the gap the view describes.

statement.text: Synthetic reading: the newer edition puts clean-technology demand in 2030 at 10,100 kt, against 9,400 kt in the earlier edition.

reasons.title: Synthetic mine supply responds slowly
reasons.plain: Synthetic: if mines add output slowly, supply stays behind demand for longer.

statement.text: Synthetic reading: the newer release puts world mine production in 2024 at 22,900 kt, against 22,700 kt in the earlier release.

reasons.title: Synthetic recycling adds little supply
reasons.plain: Synthetic: recycled metal is supply too, and more of it narrows the gap.

statement.text: Synthetic reading: the newer edition puts secondary supply in 2030 at 4,800 kt, against 4,300 kt in the earlier edition.

reasons.title: Synthetic total demand keeps rising through the projection
reasons.plain: Synthetic: demand that keeps rising within one edition's projection widens the gap the view describes.

statement.text: Synthetic reading: the same edition puts total demand at 29,500 kt in 2030 and at 31,800 kt in 2035.
